title: id(world_net): info_details reads a mistyped 'active_module_hash' as Ok(None) — a malformed module_info reply reports "no module" for a world that has one

body:
## Problem

`WorldClient::info_details` in `pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs` (reply handling at :1473 on main `075b2de904`) reads the `module_info` reply's active module hash with a bare optional coercion:

```rust
let active_module_hash = reply["active_module_hash"].as_str().map(str::to_owned);
```

`as_str()` returns `None` for **every** non-string value, so a present-but-mistyped `active_module_hash` (number, bool, array, object) is silently read as `None` — the exact value that legitimately means "this world has no installed module". The host's `ServerFrame::ModuleInfo` (`pkgs/id/src/world_session/types.rs:330-336`) always serializes this field as either a string or `null`, so a non-string, non-null value can only be corruption, a version-skewed host, or a hostile/buggy peer — and the client should say so instead of inventing "no module".

The same reply is otherwise strict, which is the in-function oracle:

- `world_id` missing/mistyped → error (`"host omitted world id"`, :1469-1472)
- `current_sequence` missing/mistyped → error (`"host omitted sequence"`, :1474-1476)
- a non-null `active_module_provenance` that fails to decode → error (`"host sent invalid module provenance"`, :1477-1482)

Only the hash field collapses malformed → absent.

## Why it matters

Consumers trust `None` as a factual statement about the world:

- `id world download` (`pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs:214-216`) turns the coerced `None` into the operator-facing claim "world has no installed module to download" — wrong diagnosis for a world that does have a module, sending debugging in the wrong direction.
- `capture_world_state` (`pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs:1148`) bakes `module_hash: info.active_module_hash` into the captured `WorldState` manifest — a mistyped reply is recorded as a manifest with **no module**, the same class of fabricated capture state as the manifest seed issue (#6626, different field/function).
- `id world info` JSON output (`commands/world.rs:665`) prints `"active_module_hash": null`, indistinguishable from a genuinely module-less world.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Probe on the laptop against main `075b2de904`, real `id` crate with a scripted iroh host (`~/git/fleet/probe-compile-wt/pkgs/id/tests/probe_info_reply.rs`, test `probe_info_reply_shapes`):

- control, string hash `"abc123"` → `Ok(Some("abc123"))`
- control, `null` hash → `Ok(None)` (the legitimate no-module case)
- mistyped hash `123` / `true` / `["abc"]` / `{"h":"abc"}` → all `Ok(None)` — silently conflated with no-module
- oracle in the same reply: mistyped non-null `active_module_provenance: 123` → `Err("host sent invalid module provenance")`

Dedup: `gh search issues` for `active_module_hash` / `info_details` / `module_info` in this repo returns no issue covering `info_details` reply validation. Neighbours are distinct functions/fields: #6620 (`compile()` reply defaults), #6621 (`read_worlds_reply` entries), #6624 (`caps()` report), #6625 (`policy_request` reply), #6626 (`manifest_state` seed), #6632 (`create_world` flag).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `info_details` errors when `active_module_hash` is present and neither a string nor `null`, with an error naming the malformed field.
- [ ] A string hash still returns `Some(hash)`; `null` (and a genuinely absent field, for older hosts) still returns `None`.
- [ ] Regression tests with a scripted host (or equivalent) covering: string, null, absent, and at least number/object mistyped shapes.
- [ ] No host-side change; `ServerFrame::ModuleInfo` serialization is unchanged.
